security_audit.summary: I confirmed one real command-execution risk in the training runner and two boundary-crossing parent-directory references in the skill instructions. The git status subprocess, Markdown backticks, and training-policy Avoid section are false positives. No evidence found for prompt injection, social engineering, or data exfiltration intent.

remediation.issue: The runner executes a selected training command in the target repository.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval for each command, keep shell execution disabled, use timeouts, and document that only trusted repositories are supported.

remediation.issue: The skill instructions reference parent-directory files outside the skill package.
remediation.suggestion: Vendor required guidance into the skill bundle or replace parent-directory references with package-local paths.

content.value_statement: Training runs often lack clear status, logs, and reproducibility evidence. This skill runs a selected command conservatively and records structured training evidence.
actual_capabilities: Runs a selected training command with a configurable monitoring timeout.
Captures stdout, stderr, exit status, timeout state, and launch failures.
Extracts epochs, steps, metrics, and checkpoint file names from logs.
Classifies results as success, partial, blocked, resumed, or verified.
Reports changed, new, and deleted files using git status snapshots.
Supports standardized train_outputs evidence for summaries, commands, logs, and status.
limitations: Does not choose research goals or design experiment sweeps.
Does not set up environments, download assets, or fix missing dependencies.
Runs only the selected command; untrusted commands can still be dangerous.
Short verification windows cannot prove full reproduction success.

use_cases.title: Verify Training Startup
use_cases.description: Run a documented command briefly and confirm whether training starts, logs steps, and reports blockers.

use_cases.title: Resume a Training Run
use_cases.description: Check a resume command, record checkpoint assumptions, and capture whether progress continues.

use_cases.title: Record Reproduction Evidence
use_cases.description: Create concise evidence for a reproduction report, including command status, metrics, checkpoints, and changed files.

prompt_templates.title: Startup Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner verification of a selected command.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run startup verification for this selected training command: [command]. Use a 120 second timeout and record evidence in train_outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Short Run Verification
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate check with dataset and checkpoint assumptions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run short-run verification for [command]. Record dataset assumptions, checkpoint source, completed steps, observed metrics, and any blocker.

prompt_templates.title: Resume Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced resume validation from a known checkpoint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume training with [command] from [checkpoint]. Capture resume status, last step, best metric, best checkpoint, and changed files.

prompt_templates.title: Full Kickoff Evidence
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced kickoff with bounded monitoring and reporting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Kick off the selected full training command with a finite monitoring window. Preserve command, config, seed, logs, status, metrics, and checkpoint evidence.

output_examples.input: Startup verification for a documented image classification training command.
output_examples.output: The summary reports that training launched, reached the first steps, found no checkpoint yet, and stopped after the planned window.

output_examples.input: Resume verification from an existing checkpoint.
output_examples.output: The evidence states the resume command, checkpoint source, last observed step, best metric, and whether any files changed.

output_examples.input: Training command fails before launch because an executable is missing.
output_examples.output: The report marks the run as blocked, names the missing executable, and records that no training progress was observed.

best_practices: Use only commands selected and approved by a trusted user.
Set a timeout that matches the verification goal.
Record dataset, checkpoint, seed, and config assumptions before running.
anti_patterns: Using the skill for open ended experiment sweeps.
Treating startup verification as full reproduction success.
Running commands from an untrusted repository without review.

faq.question: What does this skill run?
faq.answer: It runs a selected training command in a repository and captures bounded execution evidence.

faq.question: Does it choose the training command?
faq.answer: No. A user or upstream workflow must select the command before this skill runs it.

faq.question: Can it resume training?
faq.answer: Yes. It can record resume mode, checkpoint source, observed progress, and resume blockers.

faq.question: Where are outputs recorded?
faq.answer: The skill expects standardized evidence under train_outputs, including summaries, commands, logs, and status.

faq.question: Does it install dependencies?
faq.answer: No. Environment setup, downloads, and dependency repair are outside this skill.

faq.question: Is it safe with untrusted commands?
faq.answer: No. Review commands and repositories first because the runner executes the selected process.
